title: Choose the metric’s population · Predeclare acceptance
summary: Validation-only evidence for the supplied order task.

blocks.text: Which errors matter for late orders?
Choose classification metrics for class balance and the consequences and costs of false positives and false negatives, not accuracy alone.
Precision = TP/(TP+FP) is the proportion of predicted positives that are actual positives. Recall = TP/(TP+FN) is the proportion of actual positives detected.
MAE averages absolute regression errors; MSE averages squared errors, giving larger errors more influence.
Validation prevalence is actual positives divided by the validation population; use it to interpret that cohort’s metrics.
Confusion-table frequencies describe this cohort’s outcomes. They do not establish calibration of individual probability scores.

blocks.caption: Actual and predicted classes are separate.

result_of.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN predicted_label=1 THEN count ELSE 0 END) AS predicted_positive_total, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_label=1 THEN count ELSE 0 END) AS actual_positive_total, SUM(count) AS cohort_total FROM counts

blocks.text: Read precision from the predicted-positive group and recall from the actual-positive group. The displayed totals expose their different denominators. Prevalence uses the whole cohort. In the separate regression fixture, compare the absolute-error and squared-error averages: squaring gives the larger residual more influence. Choose the task metric for target type and error consequences before comparison. These cohort outcomes do not establish calibration of an individual probability score.
Precision and recall use different groups; neither proves probability-score calibration.

options.text: Cohort precision, recall and actual-positive prevalence, but not calibration of individual probability scores.
Calibration of each individual score, because precision is a conditional frequency.
Recall conditions on predicted positives, while prevalence counts predictions.

public.prompt: Create a report with this exact label order: precision (two decimals), recall (two decimals), prevalence (two decimals); then metric=recall and the interpretations shown below. Use the TP, FP, FN and TN count cells, not precomputed metrics. The task prioritizes catching actual late orders over avoiding unnecessary alerts. Report text after the numeric values must be: "; metric=recall; precision conditions on predicted positives; recall conditions on actual positives; cohort frequencies do not establish individual-score calibration; missed late orders are prioritized". Separate the numeric fields with "; ". Put the complete report in AZ2 as one formula; headers are in row 1 and all registry columns are shown in their original order.

grading.reference_formula: ="precision="&TEXT(B2/(B2+C2),"0.00")&"; recall="&TEXT(B2/(B2+D2),"0.00")&"; prevalence="&TEXT((B2+D2)/(B2+C2+D2+E2),"0.00")&"; metric=recall; precision conditions on predicted positives; recall conditions on actual positives; cohort frequencies do not establish individual-score calibration; missed late orders are prioritized"
grading.expected_value: precision=0.80; recall=0.60; prevalence=0.20; metric=recall; precision conditions on predicted positives; recall conditions on actual positives; cohort frequencies do not establish individual-score calibration; missed late orders are prioritized

blocks.text: Set the contract before results arrive.
Declare measurable predictive acceptance and the supplied deployment compatibility requirements before comparing candidates.
Keep supplied deployment class probabilities and error costs fixed; do not choose inputs to favor a result.
FPR = FP/(FP+TN) conditions on actual negatives; FNR = FN/(FN+TP) conditions on actual positives. Empty groups leave rates undefined.
With correct predictions costing zero, expected error cost = P(Y=0) × FPR × cost_FP + P(Y=1) × FNR × cost_FN.
Compare expected cost with the predeclared upper bound using <=. Operating limits are separate eligibility requirements.

result_of.sql: SELECT SUM(weighted_contribution) AS expected_error_cost, expected_cost_bound, SUM(weighted_contribution) <= expected_cost_bound AS predictive_requirement_met FROM terms CROSS JOIN contract GROUP BY expected_cost_bound

blocks.caption: Fixed predictive inputs; operating eligibility remains separate.

blocks.text: The two actual-class rows separate deployment probability, conditional error rate and error cost. Sum their weighted contributions and compare with the fixed bound. A passing predictive quantity does not resolve latency or other operating requirements. The formula assumes zero cost for correct predictions. Do not substitute validation prevalence for supplied deployment probabilities. Keep actual-class counts: an empty group leaves a required rate unresolved, not perfect.
Low predictive cost is not operating acceptance. Keep supplied probabilities and costs fixed.

public.prompt: Under zero cost for correct predictions, which predictive acceptance contract preserves the supplied fixed inputs and separate operating limits?

options.text: Require P(Y=0) × FPR × cost_FP + P(Y=1) × FNR × cost_FN <= the predeclared bound, and check operating limits separately.
Replace deployment class probabilities with whichever candidate’s validation prevalence gives the lowest cost.
Once expected cost passes, all operating limits automatically pass.

public.prompt: In Terms!AZ2 write a single formula report: FPR denominator=<actual-negative count>; FNR denominator=<actual-positive count>; expected_cost=<two decimals or undefined>; predictive_requirement=cost<=<Contract bound to two decimals>; predictive_verdict=<pass, fail or unresolved>; operating_limits=separate supplied predicates, no numeric latency bound supplied; deployment probabilities and error costs fixed before comparison. Use the supplied class probabilities, conditional rates and error costs from Terms rows 2 and 3. Guard empty conditioning groups. Compare cost to Contract!F2; do not invent operating limits or infer overall eligibility. Retain all contract inputs unchanged.

files.content: // Enter the predictive contract report in Terms!AZ2.

solution_files.content: Terms!AZ2: ="FPR denominator="&E2&"; FNR denominator="&E3&"; expected_cost="&IF(OR(E2=0,E3=0),"undefined",TEXT(B2*C2*D2+B3*C3*D3,"0.00"))&"; predictive_requirement=cost<="&TEXT(Contract!F2,"0.00")&"; predictive_verdict="&IF(OR(E2=0,E3=0),"unresolved",IF(B2*C2*D2+B3*C3*D3<=Contract!F2,"pass","fail"))&"; operating_limits=separate supplied predicates, no numeric latency bound supplied; deployment probabilities and error costs fixed before comparison"
